title: Accelerate graph shortest paths in WebAssembly
objective: Profile public Graph shortest-path, all-pairs, clique, coloring, and isomorphism workloads, then route one or two measured Python-dominant Tier-2 shortest-path workflows through a bounded source-transparent packed WebAssembly kernel with exact fallback, authenticated route evidence, differential and direct/public Node/browser tests, interrupt safety, and a benchmark

handoff.summary: Follow-on to the connected-components slice already integrated at 48eb9e84. Adds source-transparent packed single-source and all-pairs unweighted shortest-path kernels, exact public Graph fallbacks, authenticated private route evidence, deterministic bounds/work-budget cancellation, CPython/native-disabled differential coverage, direct real-Wasm plus public Node/Chromium coverage, and a public-workload benchmark. Measured medians on linux-x64 were 7.24x for CycleGraph(5000).shortest_path and 2.46x for CycleGraph(500).distances_all_pairs; clique was input-sensitive, coloring remained Python-heavy but exponential, and isomorphism already used the mature optional igraph route.
risks: The shared package graph, native-kernel inventory/capability rows, coverage corpus, and browser precompile manifest are intentionally deferred to the integration lane.

The focused Chromium test installs a private authenticated builtins bridge because the current browser runtime does not expose its resolver to sagejs.native._compiled; integration must land the shared resolver hook before removing that test-only bridge.
The conservative all-pairs limits (2048 vertices, 4000000 endpoint entries, 32 MiB output) prefer exact portable fallback for larger inputs.
next_steps: Register packed-graph-shortest-paths-production and assign src/lib/sagejs/kernels/graph/shortest_paths.py to graph-native-kernels in the shared architecture manifests.
Precompile sagejs.kernels.graph, sagejs.kernels.graph.components, and sagejs.kernels.graph.shortest_paths for the public browser runtime.
Land the central browser resolver-to-builtins hook, then remove or simplify the focused test's temporary private host bridge.
Regenerate shared coverage/capability artifacts and run the integrated architecture and browser suites.
